name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate

lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a chemically modified version of the peptide Semax. The modifications are meant to make it last longer in the body.
No studies of this exact compound are reported, and it has no studied appearance use.

paras: It is presumed to act like Semax, which is described as affecting neurotrophin (BDNF, NGF) expression in animal studies; this has not been tested for the modified form. Intranasal use is the route typically described.
It is sold for laboratory use and is not approved for human use in most jurisdictions. Safety in people has not been studied.

lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Semax, with the sequence Ac-Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, N-terminally acetylated and C-terminally amidated. These changes are described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown. [1]

It is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use and is not approved for human therapeutic use. Claimed benefits are extrapolated from Semax research; the source reports no direct studies of this variant. [1]

paras: The acetyl group at the N-terminus is described as blocking aminopeptidases, and the amide at the C-terminus as blocking carboxypeptidases. [1] The stability benefits are described as hypothesized and unverified for this specific compound. [1]
No studies found. Any clinical or animal findings relate to unmodified Semax, not this variant. [1]
